Adding a full debug from this morning, this one doesn't show the exception, but failed reconnection at 07:54.

[home-assistant_2023-07-18T12-48-57.642Z.log](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/12080805/home-assistant_2023-07-18T12-48-57.642Z.log)

Thank you for the log.

It appears that the socket connection between the API and the protocol adapter is being closed outside of the API.

I can't tell if the protocol adapter is closing it or if the host is, but the API is not intentional doing so. It is interesting that the connection appears to be closed immediately after the API sends a request for data to the protocol adapter. That may be an indication that it is the protocol adapter closing the connection as a rejection of what it received, but that's not something I have seen before outside of the login sequence.

Some other possibly relevant points:
- The integration hasn't been updated recently.
- There is at least one other report of connection issues after HA 2023.7.0.
- Both reporters appear to be running in a VM according to the diagnostic data, whereas I'm not seeing issues running embedded.

@bdraco Are you aware of any other integrations reporting socket connection issues after 2023.7.0?

> @bdraco Are you aware of any other integrations reporting socket connection issues after 2023.7.0?

I'm not aware of anything like that

> Some other possibly relevant points:
> 
> * The integration hasn't been updated recently.
> * There is at least one other report of connection issues after HA 2023.7.0.
> * Both reporters appear to be running in a VM according to the diagnostic data, whereas I'm not seeing issues running embedded.

After 2023.7.2 got released and I upgraded the HA, it started (re)misbehaving. I assumed I used the latest integration at that time.
HA is running on a VM indeed.

I upgraded back to 2023.7.2.

And here are the latest debug logs: 
[home-assistant_2023-07-20T01-33-12.833Z.log](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/12101282/home-assistant_2023-07-20T01-33-12.833Z.log)

At 20:04 the exception raised.
Since that time, I tried at 21:28 and 21:30 to switch off the pool and the pool light and it behaved the same, command it issued, but nothing happened and triggering a disconnection and reconnection. 

If I go to the Pentair ScreenLogic app, I can issue the  with no problem. Same using screenlogicpy CLI. So I assume the gateway is fine. 

Finally after that, I just rebooted the VM. I turned on the lights in HA, and off in the Pentair App, HA reflected the lights turning off. Doing this again worked. Here are the logs of this experiment: 
[home-assistant_2023-07-20T01-56-18.984Z.log](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/12101392/home-assistant_2023-07-20T01-56-18.984Z.log)

Additional information.
At midnight, a trigger to turn off the pool lights ran and segfaulting inside screenlogic. Since that moment (12 hours after the segfault event), screen logic display are not getting updates, command are not send to the gateway, screenlogic device is unresponsive and a reload is required is required (initiated at 12:12). It looks like when a segfault happen, screenlogic device cannot recover and manual intervention is necessary.

Logs: 
[home-assistant_2023-07-20T16-14-26.440Z.log](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/12111811/home-assistant_2023-07-20T16-14-26.440Z.log)

At this point, I'd like to focus on the raised exceptions here in this issue, and consolidate discussion and troubleshooting on intermittent connections in #96016.

I'll be closing this one out when the exception handling is buttoned up. Thanks for all your help!

review_comments: Its not ideal that the API would control the flow by returning `False` or raising an exception for different failure cases instead of raising (a different) exception depending on the failure type.

You're right. It's not ideal. 
Returning `False` is legacy from the original idea of simply returning the success state. Retrying requests and reconnecting have all outgrown that concept at this point. In reality exception handling in the API needs an overhaul, but I expect that to take some time and not be ready until the next major release.  

This PR was an effort to improve the end user experience in the meantime.  If it's preferred that we leave things as-is until that overhaul is complete, we can kill this.

I'm ok with this as an interim solution.

If you plan on refactoring the lib before the end of November it might be best to not merge this though so we don't have the churn of having to back it out later on when the lib is refactored.

I don't think it will be complete by the end of November. The refactor interacts with a number of new features already in progress for the next major version of the lib and it's highly unlikely it will all be buttoned up by then.
